solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fail to work, having succeeded in objection

parts.note: a machine that works is said to go

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits in the word for an objection, cutting it open

parts.note: a 'but' is an objection, as in 'no buts'
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: Someone fails at a job even though their protest was upheld.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fail to work' looks like the definition, but only 'Fail' is; 'to work' gives GO.
explanation.definitionFit: To go bust is to collapse financially, an idiom for a business failing.

clue.text: Elaborate dress: set out before noon to gain impetus

parts.note: a getup is an elaborate outfit

indicators.note: set out suggests the letters are laid out afresh, rearranged

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, means before noon

explanation.surface: Fancy clothes laid out in the morning to give a boost.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam engines need pressure to move, so getting up steam is an idiom for building momentum.

clue.text: At front of Berkeley Square picked up land

indicators.note: the front of the word Berkeley is its first letter
in a down clue, picked up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: nine is a square number, three times three

explanation.surface: At the front of a London square, something is picked up off the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Berkeley Square' reads as the London square, but Square is split off to mean a square number.
explanation.definitionFit: Benin is a country in West Africa, and land is a common crossword word for a country.

clue.text: Curious how day's dim

indicators.note: something curious is odd, so these letters are arranged oddly

explanation.surface: Wondering why the day is so gloomy.
explanation.definitionFit: Shadowy means dim or poorly lit, full of shadows.

clue.text: Run around somewhat, having small puncture

indicators.note: the word for running goes around the phrase for somewhat

parts.note: to flee is to run away
'a bit' means somewhat

explanation.surface: A runner gets a slight puncture somewhere along the course.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect's bite leaves a tiny hole in the skin, so a fleabite is literally a small puncture.

clue.text: Flat surface's length, on the side?

parts.note: an edge is a side

explanation.surface: Asking whether a level surface's length runs along its side.
explanation.definitionFit: A ledge is a narrow horizontal shelf projecting from a wall or cliff.

clue.text: Ancient city's once fantastic empty hotel?

parts.note: antic once meant fantastic; made empty, it is given O, nothing, inside it
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A city of antiquity had an extraordinary hotel that now stands vacant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' is an occasional device: the word for fantastic (ANTIC, an archaic sense flagged by 'once') is given O, nothing, inside it to make ANTIOC.
explanation.definitionFit: Antioch was a major city of the Hellenistic and Roman world, now Antakya in Turkey.

clue.text: Hard to avoid publican in possibly obscene fraud

indicators.note: the trimmed publican goes in the word for obscene

parts.note: impure can mean lewd, so obscene is possibly impure

indicators.note: the publican's word avoids the hard letter, dropping it

parts.note: a publican is the host of a pub
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A landlord steers clear of filth in a swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: An imposture is a deception, the act of passing oneself off as someone else.

clue.text: Off-white linen carried by recruits

indicators.note: the letters are carried within the word recruits

explanation.surface: Pale cloth is hauled about by new soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecru is the pale greyish-yellow colour of unbleached linen.

clue.text: Combined a line with another, no breaks

indicators.note: the word no breaks into the second line, splitting it

parts.note: another line, written out in full

explanation.surface: Joining one line to another without gaps.
explanation.definitionFit: All-in-one describes things combined into a single unit.

clue.text: Well-armed number challenged to depose king

parts.note: ten is a number

indicators.note: deposing removes a ruler, so the king's letter is taken out

parts.note: to tackle someone is to challenge them
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A numbered rival was challenged to overthrow the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: An octopus or squid is tentacled, and its many limbs make it humorously well-armed.

clue.text: Get smaller recorder

definitions.meaning: to narrow gradually towards one end
one who tapes, i.e. records sound

explanation.surface: A shrinking recording device.
explanation.definitionFit: Taper the verb means to narrow; taper the noun can jokingly mean one who records on tape.

clue.text: Double act being wordless awkwardly hampers emotion

indicators.note: done awkwardly, the letters are clumsily rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A silent comedy duo whose clumsiness gets in the way of their feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: A pantomime horse is a costume worn by two performers, a fixture of the British Christmas pantomime, a family stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: Two actors share one silent horse costume, so it is a double act that never speaks.

clue.text: Head of bank will learn to manipulate capital restriction

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
manipulating the letters moves them into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A bank chief will be taught how to handle limits on money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital restriction' suggests finance; it is a barrier in a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Berlin Wall divided the German capital, restricting movement between East and West.

clue.text: Irritable match ending in acrimony

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match

indicators.note: the ending of the word acrimony is its last letter

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered game finishes in bitterness.
explanation.definitionFit: Testy is a synonym for irritable, describing someone easily annoyed.

clue.text: Altogether the last three knockout rounds that spanned several years

parts.note: quarter-finals, semi-finals and final hold 4, 2 and 1 matches: seven in total
ties are knockout matches in a cup competition

explanation.surface: The closing knockout stages of a cup took years to complete.
explanation.walkthrough: In a knockout cup the last three rounds hold four, two and one ties, seven in all.
explanation.definitionFit: The seventies is a decade, a span covering several years.

clue.text: Hospitality for all in old luxury flat as temperature falls

indicators.note: the temperature letter falls away, dropping out of the flat's word

parts.note: a penthouse is a luxury flat on the top floor

explanation.surface: An old upmarket apartment cools down.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping open house means welcoming any visitor, i.e. offering hospitality to everyone.

clue.text: Roughly calculate what's left: about one metre

indicators.note: the estate word goes about, around, the other letters

parts.note: an estate is what a person leaves when they die
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Working out an approximate remainder of around a metre.
explanation.definitionFit: To estimate is to judge an amount approximately.

clue.text: Heedful of a green hollow in which day is advancing

indicators.note: the day letter moves forward, earlier in the word it sits in

parts.note: vert is green in heraldry
a dent is a hollow

explanation.surface: Someone careful about a green dip in the landscape as the day wears on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is advancing' moves the D of AVERTDENT forward to sit after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Advertent is the rare positive of inadvertent, meaning attentive or paying heed.

clue.text: In submarine, maybe, one who's elected to conserve oxygen is a cold fish

parts.note: a submarine is a long sandwich, made on a roll

indicators.note: conserving something holds it in, so the elected member keeps the oxygen inside

parts.note: an MP, Member of Parliament, is elected
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A politician on a submarine saving air turns out to be a cold fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'submarine' suggests the vessel, but it is the sandwich roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A rollmop is a pickled herring fillet, served cold, literally a cold fish.

clue.text: Son in good health? That's dandy

parts.note: to be well is to be in good health

explanation.surface: A boy is fit and healthy, which is just fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dandy' reads as the adjective 'great', but the answer is the noun: a swell is a fashionable man.
explanation.definitionFit: A swell is an old word for a smartly dressed man about town, a synonym of dandy.

clue.text: Viewer hugs dog tighter

indicators.note: hugging means holding close, so the viewer wraps round the dog

parts.note: a seer is one who sees
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A spectator clutches a dog more tightly.
explanation.definitionFit: Securer means more firmly fixed, the comparative of secure.

clue.text: Harriet's relatively small cathouse?

parts.note: an uncle is a relative, hence the cheeky adverb
a tom's cabin: a tom is a male cat and a cabin is a small house

explanation.surface: Someone named Harriet owns a little house for a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cathouse' must be split as cat plus house; Harriet Beecher Stowe wrote the novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The anti-slavery novel was written by Harriet Beecher Stowe, so it is Harriet's book.

clue.text: Formal wear? It may be your call

definitions.meaning: a tailcoat, worn on formal occasions
'heads or ...' is the call made at a coin toss

explanation.surface: Choosing formal clothes is up to you.
explanation.definitionFit: Tails is both a tailcoat for formal evening wear and one side of a tossed coin.

clue.text: Half-hearted shout, not on deck

indicators.note: the heart of the shout word is a double L, and half of it goes

parts.note: a bellow is a loud shout

explanation.surface: A weak cry comes from someone off the deck.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, below means beneath the deck, inside the vessel.

clue.text: Tube through Liverpool's opening

parts.note: via means through, by way of

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Taking the Underground through a Liverpool station entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tube' suggests the London Underground; it is a small glass tube.
explanation.definitionFit: A vial is a small glass container, essentially a tube for liquids.

clue.text: Distinctive phrase fool finally changes

indicators.note: the final letter of the word for fool is switched for another

parts.note: an idiot is a fool

explanation.surface: A characteristic saying finally alters the jester's tune.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is an expression peculiar to a language, whose meaning is not literal.

clue.text: Missing volume, gap occasionally vital — this is one example

indicators.note: the volume letter is missing from the word for a gap

parts.note: an interval is a gap

indicators.note: taking letters only now and then picks the alternate ones

explanation.surface: A book lost, and a hole that matters now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing' takes V from INTERVAL, leaving INTERAL; 'occasionally' takes I and A from vital.
explanation.definitionFit: Inter alia is Latin for 'among other things', the phrase used when citing one example among several.

clue.text: No jobs after this? Call to retire

definitions.meaning: taken literally, the ... is the final job a person holds
the bugle call sounded at the end of the day and at military funerals

explanation.surface: A retirement announcement: no more work after this.
explanation.definitionFit: The bugle call signals soldiers to retire for the night; literally, a final position.

clue.text: Tool gets right inside cloth

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes inside the cloth word

parts.note: a towel is a cloth

explanation.surface: A tool is tucked properly inside a piece of fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A trowel is a small hand tool for gardening or spreading mortar.
